public_rationale: On February 27, 2024, Klarna reported that its assistant handled two-thirds of customer-service chats in its first month, before the April–June 2024 assessment period [e1]. A retrospective preprint revised July 23, 2026 reports roughly 60% success for Q2 2024 models on evaluated text tasks taking humans about 1.5 hours [e2]. These results do not establish whether dependable workplace automation covered a limited or broad range of tasks during April–June 2024 [e1, e2].
limitations: Klarna's company disclosure does not independently establish successful end-to-end completion, human intervention rates or representative task coverage [e1].
The retrospective study evaluates text-task capability rather than deployed workplace automation [e2].
The claim supplies no denominator or threshold for 'many' tasks.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Generative AI does not really automate many tasks.

statement.excerpt: The reason I'm suddenly bringing up superintelligences — or AGI (artificial general intelligence) — is because throughout every defense of generative AI is a deliberate attempt to get around the problem that generative AI doesn't really automate many tasks.

from_speaker: generative AI doesn't really automate many tasks
our_interpretation: Assess the task-automation proposition, not the surrounding allegation about advocates' intentions.
The plain reading is that generative AI completes only a limited range of work tasks without people performing or repairing substantial parts of them.
Task automation is distinct from assistance, adoption, and replacement of whole jobs. High volume on one task does not establish a broad range of automated tasks.
Use April–June 2024, the latest completed quarter before publication, for this ongoing-state observation.
criteria.support_condition: Representative deployment evidence for the target period shows that reliable, end-to-end automation remained confined to a limited range of work tasks.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative evidence for the target period establishes reliable, end-to-end automation across a broad range of work tasks.

evidence.explanation: Klarna reported substantial customer-service automation, which challenges an impression of negligible practical capability. This earlier, company-reported workload equivalent neither establishes the breadth of automated tasks nor counts eliminated jobs.

The retrospective study reports roughly 60% success for 2024-Q2 models on text tasks taking humans about 1.5 hours. This is material evidence of broad capability, but selected text-task evaluations do not establish reliable automation in actual workplaces.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Representative deployment evidence for April–June 2024 measuring task variety, successful end-to-end completion, human intervention and deployment coverage, assessed against an explicit denominator and threshold for limited versus broad automation.
